answers.question: How does the FHIR2 module map an OpenMRS Patient to a FHIR Patient resource? Explain the translator and its main mappings.

paragraphs.text: OpenMRS stores a patient as a database entity (`org.openmrs.Patient`); FHIR stores it as a `Patient` resource. The FHIR2 module keeps those two worlds apart and puts a **translator** in the middle: one class that knows how to build a FHIR `Patient` out of an OpenMRS patient. Everything I describe below is in `github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-fhir2`.
## Where the translation is triggered

The FHIR REST layer is in the providers: `PatientFhirResourceProvider` handles `GET /Patient/{id}` and calls the service [1]. The service `FhirPatientServiceImpl` fetches the database record through its DAO and hands it to the translator [2]. Searches go the same way: results come back as OpenMRS patients and are mapped with the same translator [3].
The contract is the interface `PatientTranslator`, a two-way (`OpenmrsFhirUpdatableTranslator`) translator: `toFhirResource` for reading out to FHIR, `toOpenmrsType` for writing back [4].
## The main translator: `PatientTranslatorImpl`

`PatientTranslatorImpl` is a Spring `@Component` [5]. It holds no mapping logic for the small fields itself; instead it is injected with eight helper translators plus a global-property service and a person DAO [6]. That is the design idea: one translator per concept, so `Patient`, `Person` and `Practitioner` can share the same name/address/gender rules.
The read direction, `toFhirResource`, is a single pass over the OpenMRS patient [7].
## The field-by-field mappings

| FHIR `Patient` field | OpenMRS source | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `patient.getUuid()` | the UUID is the FHIR id |
| `active` | `!patient.getVoided()` | voided = inactive |
| `identifier` | active `PatientIdentifier`s | one FHIR `Identifier` each |
| `name` | every `PersonName` | given/middle/family + extensions |
| `gender` | `patient.getGender()` | M→male, F→female, U→unknown, O→other |
| `birthDate` | `patient.getBirthdate()` | precision reduced if estimate |
| `deceased[x]` | `getDead()` + `getDeathDate()` | boolean or dateTime |
| `address` | every `PersonAddress` | city, state, country, district, postal |
| `telecom` | person attributes of a configured type | e.g. phone numbers |
| `extension` | every `PersonAttribute` | OpenMRS-only attributes |
| `meta.lastUpdated` / `meta.versionId` | audit dates | version = timestamp in millis |
The UUID is also copied into `Patient.id` [8], which is what makes a FHIR URL and an OpenMRS record refer to the same person.

**Identifiers.** The patient's *active* identifiers are looped over and each is mapped by `PatientIdentifierTranslatorImpl` [9]. That helper sets the value, sets `use` to `official` when the identifier is the preferred one and `usual` otherwise, derives a `system` URI from the *identifier type* (for example an OpenMRS ID vs a national ID), puts the type UUID in `type.coding.code`, and stashes the issuing location in a custom extension [10]. A voided identifier translates to `null` [11].

**Names.** Every `PersonName` becomes a `HumanName` [12]. `PersonNameTranslatorImpl` puts the given name and middle name in `given`, the family name in `family`, and the free-text `text` from `getFullName()` [13]. OpenMRS name parts that FHIR has no field for — `prefix`, `familyNamePrefix`, `familyName2`, `familyNameSuffix`, `degree` — are carried as private sub-extensions under the `.../ext/name` extension URL [14].

**Gender.** `GenderTranslatorImpl` is a plain switch over the one-letter OpenMRS codes, defaulting to `NULL` for anything unrecognised [15]. The main translator only calls it when a gender is actually set [16].

**Birth date.** This is the cleverest mapping, because OpenMRS allows *estimated* birthdates. If the birthdate is not estimated, a plain full date is used; if it is estimated, the accuracy is deliberately coarsened — only the year for anyone older than 5, and only year+month for children up to 5 [17]. FHIR expresses this through the date's precision (e.g. `2001` or `2001-06`), so no precision is claimed that OpenMRS does not have. On the way back the rule is inverted: day precision clears `birthdateEstimated`, month/year precision sets it [18].

**Deceased.** If the patient is dead and a death date exists, `deceasedDateTime` is set; if they are dead with no recorded date, `deceasedBoolean` is `true`; otherwise `deceasedBoolean` is explicitly `false` [19].

**Addresses.** Each `PersonAddress` is mapped by `PersonAddressTranslatorImpl`, which lines up the overlapping fields — `cityVillage`→`city`, `stateProvince`→`state`, `countyDistrict`→`district`, plus country and postal code — and marks a preferred address as `use = home`, otherwise `old` [20]. The numbered OpenMRS address lines (`address1`..`address15`), which a country-specific address hierarchy uses, are packed into the `.../ext/address` extension by the shared `BaseAddressTranslator` [21].

**Telecom.** FHIR contact points are not a first-class OpenMRS concept, so the module uses an attribute-based convention: a global property (`fhir2.personContactPointAttributeTypeUuid` [22]) names the person attribute type that holds phone/email values. If it is unset, no telecom entries are produced; otherwise the person's active attributes of that type are loaded via `FhirPersonDao` and mapped to `ContactPoint`s [23]. The DAO query filters on the person, the attribute type UUID and non-voided rows [24]. `TelecomTranslatorImpl` fills in value and id, and copies `system`/`use`/`rank` from a configurable mapping table (`FhirContactPointMap`) so that, for instance, a "Telephone" attribute becomes `system = phone` [25].

**Person attributes as extensions.** OpenMRS lets a site define arbitrary extra fields on a person; FHIR has no such field. Each attribute therefore becomes a nested `.../ext/person-attribute` extension containing the attribute *type name* and a typed *value* extension [26]. The value is typed from the attribute type's format: string, boolean, a `Reference` to a Location, or a `CodeableConcept` from a Concept; unsupported formats are logged and dropped [27]. The main translator adds an extension only when one was produced [28].

**Metadata.** `meta.lastUpdated` uses `dateChanged` if present else `dateCreated`, and `meta.versionId` is that date as epoch milliseconds, which gives FHIR clients optimistic-concurrency versions [29] [30].
## The reverse direction

`toOpenmrsType` walks the FHIR resource and writes into an OpenMRS patient: UUID from `id`, then identifiers, names (matched by name `id` to an existing `PersonName` so renames update rather than duplicate [31]), gender, birthdate, deceased, addresses, telecom (turned back into person attributes of the configured type), and the person-attribute extensions, warning on invalid ones [32]. One asymmetry worth knowing: `active` is read out but not written back, and names/addresses are appended rather than reconciled except by UUID [33].
## What I did and did not check

I read the translator, all its injected helpers named above, the R4 provider, the service impl, the constants and the person DAO. I did not read the DAO base classes (`BasePersonDao`), the search-query machinery, or the R3 provider, and I did not check the other four repositories — they are unrelated to this mapping. The unit test `PatientTranslatorImplTest` exists and documents expected behaviour, but I only saw its name in search results, not its contents.
